title: Validate Transaction Request Sequence
real_world_story: A banking system records transaction actions using symbols to represent opening and closing stages of operations. Before processing a request, the system must verify that all stages are properly ordered and closed.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Encoded opening and closing transaction operations
real_world_connection.target_represents: Whether the transaction sequence is properly balanced
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: A stack used to match every closing operation with its corresponding opening operation

problem_statement: Given a string containing the characters '(', ')', '[', ']', '{', and '}', determine whether the sequence of transaction operations is valid. A sequence is valid if every opening symbol is closed by the correct type of closing symbol in the proper order.
task: Determine whether the given transaction operation sequence is valid.
input_format: The input contains a single string consisting only of the characters '(', ')', '[', ']', '{', and '}'.
output_format: Print YES if the sequence is valid. Otherwise, print NO.

examples.explanation: Every opening operation has the correct closing operation in the proper nested order.
The closing brackets do not match the corresponding opening brackets in the required order.

expected_algorithm.name: Stack
expected_algorithm.reason: A stack follows Last-In-First-Out ordering, allowing the most recently opened operation to be matched with its closing operation.

hint: Push every opening symbol onto a stack.
When a closing symbol appears, check the top of the stack.
The closing symbol must match the most recently opened symbol.
The sequence is valid only when the stack is empty at the end.
real_world_takeaway: Stack-based validation helps transaction systems verify that nested operations are completed in the correct order before processing them.
